j particle: a neutral meson with a large mass
j. b. s. haldane: Scottish geneticist (son of John Haldane) who contributed to the development of population genetics; a popularizer of science and a Marxist (1892-1964)
j. c. maxwell: Scottish physicist whose equations unified electricity and magnetism and who recognized the electromagnetic nature of light (1831-1879)
j. craig ventner: United States geneticist who published the complete base sequences for all the genes of a free-living organism, the influenza bacterium; later led team that developed a first draft of the entire human genome (born in 1946)
j. e. johnston: Confederate general in the American Civil War; led the Confederate troops in the West (1807-1891)
j. edgar hoover: United States lawyer who was director of the FBI for 48 years (1895-1972)
j. m. barrie: Scottish dramatist and novelist; created Peter Pan (1860-1937)
j. m. synge: Irish poet and playwright whose plays are based on rural Irish life (1871-1909)
j. r. firth: English linguist who contributed to linguistic semantics and to prosodic phonology and who was noted for his insistence on studying both sound and meaning in context (1890-1960)
j.r.r. tolkien: British philologist and writer of fantasies (born in South Africa) (1892-1973)
